text:
Recommendation: Don't shut down the note app and pivot fully. Instead, build AI agents into the existing product first and validate the new idea before committing the whole team.
Why:
- You'd be giving up $16,000/month (~$192K/year) in real recurring revenue that most pre-seed AI startups would envy.
- 2% monthly churn (~22% annually) is healthy for SMB B2B SaaS — customers are staying because the product works.
- Your 40 paying teams are a distribution channel and feedback source that won't follow you to a new product after shutdown.
- "Investors love it" isn't a strategy; investors fund traction, and a 4-person team starting from zero in the most crowded software category is a weaker pitch than $192K ARR plus an AI expansion story.
- "AI agent platform" isn't yet a defined product — unclear customer, job-to-be-done, or differentiation from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Salesforce, and many funded startups.
- Your existing teams' data is the context agents need — an advantage most agent startups lack.
- Shutting down is nearly impossible to undo, while pivoting is easy to reverse if the note app stays alive.
Risks and unknowns: What's actually driving this — stalled growth, fundraising pressure, or the team losing interest in notes? That answer changes the analysis. A full pivot could make sense if the note app has flatlined for months, if $16K/month can't cover the team and money is running out, or if specific agent customers are already pulling you that way.
Next steps:
1. Build agent features into the note app (e.g., turning meeting notes into tasks/follow-ups/CRM updates, or answering questions across a team's knowledge) and charge for it as an add-on; let the 40 teams validate it within weeks.
2. Keep the note app running lean — one person on maintenance/support part-time, three people exploring the agent idea.
3. Run 15–20 interviews with target agent buyers and aim for 3–5 letters of intent or paid pilots before committing further.
4. Set an explicit kill criterion for the note app (e.g., wind it down once agent add-on revenue passes a set threshold or growth stalls for a defined number of months).
